Tetracycline and Midazolam (Intranasal): Tetracycline increases the systemic exposure of intranasal midazolam by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction may prolong sedation. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 2. Bismuth Subsalicylate and Minocycline: Bismuth subsalicylate reduces the absorption of minocycline in the gastrointestinal tract, leading to decreased drug levels. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 3. Mipomersen and Tetracycline: Coadministration of these drugs may increase the risk of hepatotoxicity due to their potential to elevate hepatic enzyme levels. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) closely. 4. Mitotane and Tetracycline: Mitotane, a strong inducer of CYP3A4, reduces the levels of tetracycline by enhancing its metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust dosages as needed when coadministered. 5. Metronidazole and Montelukast: Metronidazole increases the levels of montelukast by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 6. Bismuth Subsalicylate and Nadolol: This combination may cause severe hypertension due to pharmacodynamic synergism, specifically through the inhibition of renal prostaglandin synthesis. Use caution and monitor blood pressure closely. 7. Nafcillin and Tetracycline: Nafcillin reduces the levels of tetracycline by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, tetracycline decreases the efficacy of nafcillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 8. Tetracycline and Naloxegol: Tetracycline increases the levels of naloxegol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 9. Metronidazole and Naloxegol: Metronidazole also increases naloxegol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 10. Metronidazole and Nateglinide: Metronidazole increases the levels of nateglinide by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Bismuth Subsalicylate and Nebivolol: This combination may lead to severe hypertension due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor blood pressure closely. 12. Metronidazole and Nelfinavir: Metronidazole increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Tetracycline and Nilotinib: Tetracycline increases nilotinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Tetracycline and Niacin: Tetracycline reduces niacin levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 15. Metronidazole and Nicardipine: Metronidazole increases nicardipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Metronidazole and Nimodipine: Metronidazole increases nimodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 17. Tetracycline and Niraparib: Tetracycline increases niraparib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 18. Metronidazole and Niraparib: Metronidazole also increases niraparib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 19. Tetracycline and Omaveloxolone: Tetracycline increases omaveloxolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 100 mg/day and monitor for adverse effects. 20. Metronidazole and Omaveloxolone: Metronidazole increases omaveloxolone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 100 mg/day and monitor for adverse effects. 21. Omeprazole and Bismuth Subsalicylate: Omeprazole increases bismuth subsalicylate levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 22. Ondansetron and Metronidazole: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution, especially with intravenous ondansetron doses exceeding 16 mg. Monitor closely for cardiac effects. 23. Tetracycline and Oxacillin: Tetracycline reduces the efficacy of oxacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 24. Metronidazole and Paclitaxel: Metronidazole increases paclitaxel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 25. Tetracycline and Palbociclib: Tetracycline increases palbociclib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Tetracycline and Pancuronium: Tetracycline enhances the effects of pancuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 27. Metronidazole and Pimozide: Metronidazole increases pimozide levels by inhibiting its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of serious adverse effects. 28. Tetracycline and Penicillin G or VK: Tetracycline reduces the efficacy of penicillin G and VK through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 29. Metronidazole and Pazopanib: Metronidazole increases pazopanib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors if possible. If unavoidable, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. 30. Tetracycline and Phenobarbital: Phenobarbital reduces tetracycline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 31. Metronidazole and Phenytoin: Metronidazole increases phenytoin levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Conversely, phenytoin reduces tetracycline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 32. Tetracycline and Phenindione: Tetracycline enhances the effects of phenindione through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 33. Metronidazole and Pioglitazone: Metronidazole increases pioglitazone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 34. Tetracycline and Piperacillin: Tetracycline reduces the efficacy of piperacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely.
